dataset_metadata.name: Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols for batteries with machine learning
dataset_metadata.institution: Stanford University; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Toyota Research Institute; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
dataset_metadata.citation: Attia, P.M., Grover, A., Jin, N. et al. Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols for batteries with machine learning. Nature 578, 397-402 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1994-5

cell_info.cell_notes: Packing date 2015-09-26, lot number EL1508007-R. Graphite anode electrode 40 um thick; LFP cathode electrode 80 um thick (from X-ray tomography). Manufacturer recommended fast-charging protocol is 3.6C (3.96 A) CC-CV. Upper and lower cutoff voltages are 3.6 V and 2.0 V respectively.

aging_modes.notes: 224 unique six-step, 10-minute fast-charging protocols in CC1-CC2-CC3-CC4 format covering 0-80% SOC. Dataset organized in 5 batches of ~48 cells each: 4 CLO batches (oed_0 through oed_3, cycled 100-120 cycles) and 1 validation batch (batch9, cycled to failure). A separate training set of 41 batteries cycled to failure was used for early-outcome predictor development. EOL defined as discharge capacity falling below 80% of nominal (0.88 Ah). Four CLO rounds were run sequentially (4 days per round, 48 parallel experiments). A total of 192 batteries were tested in the CLO budget plus 45 validation batteries. Note: dataset updated 2021-06-16 to correct minor glitches in test time during data export.

time_protocol.test_equipment: 48-channel Arbin LBT potentiostat; Amerex Instruments forced convection temperature chamber
time_protocol.notes: CLO experiment completed in 16 days (4 rounds x 4 days per round, 48 parallel cells). Each cycle consists of charging, discharging, and resting; estimated at ~1 hour per cycle. Five-second rest between charge and discharge half-cycles. Cells in CLO batches ran 100-120 cycles. Validation cells ran to failure (cycle life ~500-900+ cycles depending on protocol).

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Temperature measurements only available for validation batch (batch9). Temperature measured via Type T thermocouple with thermal epoxy and Kapton tape on exposed cell can; contact may vary substantially. MATLAB struct per batch loadable in MATLAB or Python (h5py); raw data also available as CSV per cell.
rawdata.known_issues: Four experiments did not reach 100 cycles due to contact issues (channels 17 and 27 in oed_0; channels 4 and 5 in oed_1). One protocol per round not selected due to processing error (49th-highest protocol selected instead of top-48). Three tests returned anomalous early predictions and were excluded (channel 12 in oed_0; channel 12 in oed_2; channel 6 in oed_3). One test in validation returned anomalous prediction and was excluded (channel 12, 3.6C-6.0C-5.6C-4.755C).

checkup.notes: Internal resistance measured during charging at 80% SOC by averaging 10 pulses of +/-3.6C with a pulse width of 33 ms. After fast-charge cycling, all cells recharged from 80% to 100% SOC with a 1C CC-CV step to 3.6 V (C/20 cutoff), then discharged at 4C CC-CV to 2.0 V (C/20 cutoff). Discharge capacity recorded each cycle.

notes: This dataset supports the closed-loop optimization (CLO) paper combining Bayesian optimization with early cycle-life prediction (elastic net regression on first 100 cycles) to efficiently identify high-cycle-life fast-charging protocols among 224 candidates. The dataset is closely related to the Severson et al. 2019 (Nat. Energy) dataset which provided the 41-cell training set for the early predictor. Cycle life is defined as the number of cycles until discharge capacity falls below 80% of nominal (0.88 Ah). The charging protocols are multi-step constant-current (MCC) with 5 steps: CC1 (0-20% SOC), CC2 (20-40% SOC), CC3 (40-60% SOC), CC4 (60-80% SOC, derived from constraint that total 0-80% SOC charge time = 10 min), followed by 1C CC-CV from 80% to 100% SOC. All cells discharge at 4C. Upper cutoff voltage for all steps is 3.6 V.
